thread:
Riley: Heads-up 
We've been getting complaints about the mini-playground on mobile: during streaming the token badge bounces and the pause/stop control disappears under the quick-actions row. Also, clicking a prompt from the library sometimes kills the ongoing stream. Short clip in the thread.
Sam: Drop the clip? want to see the bounce.
Riley: https://files.internal/s/playground-mobile-bounce.mp4 
Clip shows token badge shifting left-right as partial tokens come in. Stop is there for a split second then hidden when the quick-actions animate.
Leah: Sounds like two issues: (1) token counter updates on every partial chunk -> causes layout shifts; (2) prompt insert triggers full composer replace rather than patch -> stream loses session. For (1) we can render the counter in a fixed-width container so numbers don't change element width, and throttle visual updates.
Nico: Throttle idea: aggregate incoming token counts and update UI at most once per 120ms. Backend emits chunk metadata anyway, so client-side debounce is fine. That reduces layout thrash and CPU.
Jo: Fixed-width digit container is a good low-effort fix. Example CSS: 
```css
.token-badge {
  min-width: 5ch; /* reserve space for 99999 */
  text-align: right;
}
```
Leah: For prompt library inserts, instead of re-rendering the whole composer, we should do an insertText API that updates the textarea value and caret, leaving the streaming websocket session intact. That avoids server-side restart.
Riley: UX question: should the stop control float above the quick-actions or should quick-actions collapse? On tiny widths it's not obvious which is better. Mobile users care most about an obvious stop affordance.
Sam: Leaning towards a floating circular stop/pause that overlays the content at the top-right of the message area. Always visible, hits the same z-layer as floating attachments. Ensure it has a clear haptic target (44px).
Jo: Accessibility: visible label + aria-label. If visible is just an icon, aria-label should be "Stop generation". Also ensure its reachable by keyboard and reachable via screen reader rotor. For streaming text, an aria-live="assertive" is risky; prefer polite but add a control that reads last chunk on demand.
Leah: Good call. We'll expose a "Read latest" button that focuses the last chunk in an aria-live region when pressed so screen readers can replay.
Nico: Implementation plan: 1) add CSS min-width to token badge + render placeholder digits to avoid width changes, 2) debounce UI updates to 120ms, 3) implement insertText API for prompt lib, 4) add floating stop with 44px touch target and aria-label, 5) add "Read latest" affordance.
Riley: Can someone mock the visual and share a quick prototype? If design-bot can spin a preview that'd be ideal.
design-bot: Prototype created: https://playground.internal/protos/preview-578 (mobile + keyboard tests included). Visual diffs in PR comments.
Sam: I'll pick up the debounce + token-badge CSS today. Nico, can you own insertText API?
Nico: Yep, will PR the minimal DOM patch approach. Will try to keep stream session id pinned and not re-request generation on insert.
Jo: I'll write the a11y checklist and test matrix (VoiceOver, TalkBack, NVDA). Also will check high-contrast and zoom levels.
Leah: Let's run manual regression on desktop with streaming off too; we don't want the floating control to obscure compose tools. Maybe hide floating stop when not streaming.
Riley: Cool. If the prototype looks good, we'll push to a small beta users list. Recording action items on the board now.
Sam: Pairing with Jo at 2pm for a11y pass.
Riley: Thanks everyone. Keeping this thread open for updates.
